cards.text: Jesus just told a crowd about a rich man who planned bigger barns for all his stuff, until God said his life would be required of him that very night. Now Jesus turns to His disciples and says, “Therefore I tell you, do not worry about your life, what you will eat, or about your body, what you will wear.” Do not worry? Friend, for YEARS worrying was my whole personality.

cards.question: Jesus gives the disciples a reason not to worry about eating and wearing: life is more than ___, and the body more than ___.

cards.text: Then Jesus says to consider the ravens: they don't sow or reap, and they have no storehouse or barn. No barn, no apron, no oven timer, and that bird STILL worries less than I ever did.

cards.question: Jesus says the ravens go hungry because they have no storehouse or barn.
God feeds the ravens. What does Jesus say about the disciples compared to those birds?

answers.text: They are more valuable than the birds
They need far less than the birds
They should worry less than the birds

cards.text: Then Jesus asks, “Who of you by worrying can add a single hour to his life?” I worried in the back of a junk drawer for YEARS, friend, and all it ever added was dust.

cards.question: Jesus calls adding a single hour to your life by worrying a small thing.
Nobody can add even one hour to his life by worrying. So what does Jesus ask the disciples?

answers.text: Why ask God for more time

cards.text: Now Jesus says to consider how the lilies grow: they don't labor or spin. No job, no boss, no clocking in, and they STILL look better than me in this hat.

cards.question: Jesus says one lily is adorned better than a famous king in all his glory. Which king?

cards.text: Then Jesus says God clothes the grass of the field, which is here today and tomorrow is thrown into the furnace. Here today, furnace tomorrow. That's every batch I ever forgot the timer on.

cards.question: If God clothes grass that is gone by tomorrow, what does Jesus say God will do for the disciples?

cards.text: Jesus comes back around: don't be concerned about what you'll eat or drink. Don't worry about it, He says, and I think by now the disciples are getting the message LOUD and clear.

cards.question: Jesus says the Gentiles of the world strive after food and drink. What does He say about the disciples' Father?

answers.text: He wants them to strive harder
He will make them wait first

cards.question: Instead of striving after all these things, what does Jesus tell the disciples to seek?
Jesus says that if the disciples seek His kingdom, these things will be added unto them.

cards.text: Then Jesus says, “Do not be afraid, little flock.” I've been called a lot of things, friend, but with this mustache, little has NEVER been one of them.

cards.question: Jesus tells His little flock not to be afraid, because their Father is pleased to give them the ___.

cards.text: Then Jesus tells them to sell their possessions and give to the poor. I was a 25-cent stamper, friend, and SOMEBODY ELSE paid the quarter.

cards.question: Jesus tells the disciples to provide themselves with purses that will not wear out. What goes in them?
Jesus says no thief can approach that treasure in heaven, but a moth still can.
Jesus gives one more reason. He says something will always be wherever your treasure is. What is it?

cards.text: And that's where we'll leave it for now. Keep your apron on, friend, because Jesus isn't done teaching this crowd.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 5 quotes "Do not be afraid, little flock.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The opening card has four sentences: the recap of the rich man, the quote of verse 22, "Do not worry?" and the joke. The limit is three.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on. If the passage starts in the middle of a thought, it gives the context.

findings.problem: The question gives away both blanks. It says Jesus is talking about "eating and wearing," and card 1 just quoted "what you will eat" and "what you will wear." That makes food and clothes obvious, and money, work and rest are out before the baker has to think.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Multiple choice takes 5 of the stop's 8 choice cards, against 2 true or false and 1 fill in the blank. Cards 8, 10 and 12 are multiple choice in a row after card 5.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: Verse 28 is conditional: "If that is how God clothes the grass of the field." The card drops the "if" and says flatly, "Jesus says God clothes the grass of the field."
Verse 28 ends with Jesus' rebuke, "O you of little faith!" No card in the walkthrough mentions it, so the baker misses a key detail of the teaching.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The joke's action doesn't match the verse. Verse 33 is about selling your possessions and giving to the poor. "Somebody else paid the quarter" is about being bought cheaply, so the punchline doesn't click with giving. The 25-cent price also isn't set up in this lesson, so the line has to be explained.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: "What goes in them?" adds a connection the text doesn't make. In verse 33, "purses that will not wear out" and "an inexhaustible treasure in heaven" stand side by side. The text never says the treasure goes inside the purses.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The question says your heart will "always" be wherever your treasure is. Verse 34 says only "there your heart will be also." "Always" goes beyond the text.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: The closing line says Jesus isn't done teaching "this crowd." The whole passage is spoken to His disciples (Luke 12:22), and stop 1, card 1 says so.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.
